Your customers find agent failures before you do

Agents abort mid-task

Incomplete tool chains and unhandled exceptions leave work half-done. Customers see broken outcomes. Your dashboards still look green.

Loops that never end

Stuck retries and slow tool calls burn time and tokens while the user waits. Latency spikes show up in tickets, not alerts.

Frustrated users first

Off-topic or low-quality replies hit sentiment long before infra monitors fire. Support hears about it. You don't.

Budget burns quietly

Simple tasks run on expensive models. Spend climbs with no clear owner until finance asks what changed.

Paying for the same prompt twice

Identical calls fire over and over with no cache. Latency and token cost stack up with nothing useful to show for it.

Conversations that never converge

Prompt loops and circular reasoning drag sessions into endless turns. Users churn. You find out from churn reports.

Agents fail differentlyTraditional observability wasn't built for this

Agent workloads expose three gaps that request-centric stacks never solved.

01

The run you need is already gone

Full prompt and tool-call payloads make storage costs spike fast. Most stacks push teams to sample, so the failure you need later was dropped.

02

Finding one bad run takes forever

Debugging starts with questions about prompts, tools, customers, and model changes. On request-centric indexes, those searches take minutes, not seconds.

03

Infra alerts stay quiet

Wrong tool picks, loops, and fake "I did it" replies rarely trip monitors. Issues show up in support tickets long before they show up in dashboards.

A new database built from the ground up for agent traces

Object storage for retention. Serverless compute for queries. Built for agent workloads, not bolted onto a request-centric stack.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why did you build a new agent observability platform?

Teams operating agents in production kept hitting the same jobs: keep every execution, find any execution, and detect failures before customers do. Oodle is built around those workflows, not another standalone tracing silo.

Why not use OpenTelemetry, ClickHouse, and Grafana?

Those are excellent building blocks, and many customers already use them. Oodle layers an opinionated production workflow on top: full-fidelity retention, production-scale search, continuous analysis, online evals, and AI-native debugging in one place.

How is Oodle different from standalone LLM tools?

Standalone tools create another data silo. Oodle shows your LLM spans inside the same traces as your API, database, and cache calls, and addresses the full production job: retaining, searching, and continuously analyzing agent behavior on an architecture built for AI-native workloads.

Why focus on silent failures?

Agents often fail without crashing: hallucinations, wrong tools, loops, quiet regressions. Those rarely trip infra alerts, but they hit users first.

Why is search different for AI agents?

Debugging starts with questions about prompts, tools, customers, and model changes. Searching that surface across millions of executions needs a different architecture than classic request tracing.
